examples.title: A Tailwind v3 dashboard where only 13% of values use the tokens
examples.prompt: Find the hardcoded colors and magic numbers that should be using our design tokens, and fix the safe ones.
examples.summary: A small app with a Tailwind v3 config, CSS custom properties and legacy SCSS variables, plus drift planted in five flavors: near-miss hex, 15px against a 16px token, Tailwind arbitrary values, JSX inline styles and an oklch() near-match. The scan finds 48 EXACT, 10 NEAR and 14 OFF-SCALE values. --fix rewrites the 41 provably safe ones (Tailwind classes, var(), $scss and JSX strings), lists the 3 swaps that will now follow dark mode, and lifts the score from 13% to 63%. Reviewing the near misses with --fix=near takes it to 74%; what is left is off-scale values and cases that need a human.
examples.result: Drift score 13% → 63% with --fix (41 EXACT values) → 74% with --fix=near

media.alt: The top of report.md: a 13% drift-score gauge, a table of 48 EXACT, 10 NEAR and 14 OFF-SCALE values, and a near-miss color table where each found color sits next to its token in a pair of swatches that look identical, with ΔE between 0.13 and 0.53.
media.caption: report.md: six near-miss colors, each shown beside the token it should have been. Every pair is under ΔE 1, so nobody could see the difference by eye.

media.alt: Terminal: the --fix --dry-run diff turns rounded-[8px] px-[16px] into rounded-lg px-4 in Button.jsx and padding 15px 24px into 15px var(--space-6) in global.css, warns that 3 replacements will follow dark mode, then --fix prints 13% → 63% and --fix=near prints 63% → 74%.
media.caption: --fix --dry-run first, then apply. text-[14px] and the off-scale 15px are left alone on purpose.

media.alt: Terminal summary of the scan: 13% drift score, EXACT 48, NEAR 10, OFF-SCALE 14, and six near misses with true-color swatches, for example #2563ea → var(--color-brand-500) ΔE 0.13.
media.caption: The terminal summary prints the same near misses with true-color swatches.

examples.title: shadcn-style components full of p-[13px] and bg-[oklch(…)]
examples.prompt: Clean up the Tailwind arbitrary values like p-[13px] and text-[#0a0a0a] in our components.
examples.summary: A Tailwind v4 notes app with shadcn-style semantic tokens: light values in :root, dark overrides in .dark, mapped through @theme inline, plus one fixed brand color in @theme. Its components hard-code the same values as arbitrary classes, in hex and in oklch. --fix maps 49 of them to canonical classes (bg-[oklch(0.577_0.245_27.325)] → bg-destructive, rounded-[14px] → rounded-xl via calc(var(--radius) + 4px), padding: 12px → calc(var(--spacing) * 3), text-[14px] → text-[length:var(--text-sm)] so the line height is not changed) and moves the score from 18% to 85%. The 15 swaps whose token changes in dark mode are listed for confirmation. p-[13px], text-[13px] and text-[15px] sit midway between two steps and are left for a human.
examples.result: Drift score 18% → 85%; 15 of the 49 fixes flagged as theme-aware

media.alt: Terminal: the dry-run diff for button.tsx replaces bg-[oklch(0.577_0.245_27.325)] with bg-destructive, border-[oklch(0.922_0_0)] with border-border and text-[14px] with text-[length:var(--text-sm)], then a yellow warning lists 15 replacements whose token changes per theme, then --fix prints 18% → 85%.
media.caption: Raw oklch and hex become semantic classes. The yellow list names every swap that will now follow dark mode.

media.alt: The exact-matches table in report.md with swatches: hover:bg-[#f5f5f5] and bg-[oklch(0.97_0_0)] → bg-accent, text-[#0a0a0a] → text-foreground, text-[#737373] → text-muted-foreground, rounded-[6px] → rounded-sm, while text-[#a1a1a1] is held back because its exact match, --color-ring, is meant for borders.
media.caption: report.md: the same color written as hex and as oklch maps to one token. text-[#a1a1a1] is held back because its exact match is a ring color.

examples.title: A 2019 codebase with no tokens at all
examples.prompt: We don't have design tokens yet. Suggest a starter palette and spacing scale from what the code already uses.
examples.summary: A bakery ordering app written with CSS modules and styled-components, with 119 hard-coded design values and no tokens anywhere. tokens.mjs says so plainly, the scan scores it 0% without pretending any category has a score, and --propose clusters the values into candidate tokens: #333333, #323232 and #343434 become one --color-gray-700; #e5e5e5, #e6e6e6 and #e7e7e7 become one --color-gray-200; 15px folds into 16px and 180ms into 200ms. Only clusters used at least twice are proposed (25 of them); the 19 values used once are listed as one-offs instead of becoming tokens. Names follow Tailwind's palette, so the brand orange #e8590c comes out as --color-orange-600, and pure white stays --color-white instead of swallowing #f5f5f5 and #fafafa. After saving the proposal as src/tokens.css, --fix rewrites 87 values and the score goes from 0% to 74%. The names are still only a starting point: rename them to your roles before they ship.
examples.result: 119 raw values → 25 proposed tokens + 19 one-offs; adopting them takes the score from 0% to 74%

media.alt: The "Proposed tokens" table in report.md with swatches: --color-orange-600 #e8590c; --color-gray-700 #333333 absorbs #333333×5, #323232 and #343434; --color-white #ffffff stands alone; --color-gray-200 #e5e5e5 absorbs #e6e6e6 and #e7e7e7; --space-16 absorbs 15px; --font-size-14 absorbs 13px and 15px.
media.caption: report.md: each proposed token lists the near-duplicate values it would replace. White does not absorb the off-whites.

media.alt: Terminal: tokens.mjs reports no design tokens found; scan.mjs --propose shows a 0% score and the top 10 of 25 proposed tokens, notes that 19 values used once are left out as one-offs, and suggests saving the proposal and re-running; after saving it as src/tokens.css, --fix rewrites 87 values in 7 files and the score goes from 0% to 74%.
media.caption: From no tokens to a starter set: propose, approve the clusters, then let --fix swap them in.
